A.text: A service level measures agreed aspects of quality but does not necessarily represent all perceived quality
A.rationale: Service level metrics do not always cover the whole experience and set of needs.

B.text: Service level and service quality are always strictly synonymous
B.rationale: Quality is broader than the set of metrics selected.

C.text: Service quality is determined only by SLA penalties
C.rationale: Contractual penalties do not define a service's ability to meet needs.

D.text: A service level cannot contain any technical measure
D.rationale: Technical measures can be included when they are relevant to the expected quality.

181.scenario: A transformation creates new roles, but decision-making authorities remain unclear and teams use incompatible communication channels.
181.question_text: Which aspect of the "organizations and people" dimension must be tackled as a priority?
181.explanation: This dimension includes structures, authority systems, responsibilities, culture, and communication. Defining job titles alone is not enough to enable effective collaboration.

A.text: Clarify responsibilities, authorities, and communication mechanisms
A.rationale: The difficulties described directly concern the organisation of work and decisions.

B.text: Immediately buy a new monitoring tool
B.rationale: A tool alone does not resolve ambiguity around responsibilities and authority.

C.text: Renegotiate every supplier contract
C.rationale: The scenario does not mainly point to supplier relationships.

D.text: Add more steps to the workflow
D.rationale: Additional steps risk making the lack of clarity worse.

182.scenario: A team selects a very high-performance platform, but it is incompatible with the existing architecture, the available skills, and the data protection requirements.
182.question_text: Which approach best fits the "information and technology" dimension?
182.explanation: The technology choice must take into account architecture, information, skills, security, and regulatory constraints. A product's isolated performance is not enough.

A.text: Evaluate compatibility with architecture, skills, and security and compliance requirements
A.rationale: The dimension requires analysis of the whole information and technology ecosystem.

B.text: Choose the platform solely on the basis of its maximum speed
B.rationale: High performance does not compensate for the incompatibilities and risks described.

C.text: Push every constraint to partners after purchase
C.rationale: Constraints must be analysed before the decision and cannot all be transferred.

D.text: Assume the chosen technology will automatically determine the processes
D.rationale: Processes and technologies must be designed coherently, without automatic determinism.

183.scenario: An organisation hesitates between developing a capability in-house and entrusting it to a specialised supplier.
183.question_text: Which set of factors should mainly guide its sourcing strategy?
183.explanation: The sourcing decision depends notably on strategic direction, costs, resource availability, required expertise, culture, external constraints, and demand variations.

A.text: Strategic direction, available expertise, costs, culture, constraints, and demand patterns
A.rationale: These factors enable a balanced evaluation of using partners.

B.text: Only the unit price proposed by the supplier
B.rationale: Price covers neither risks, expertise, nor strategic alignment.

C.text: Only the number of suppliers present in the market
C.rationale: Market availability is one factor, but it is not enough to determine the strategy.

D.text: Only the personal preference of the technical manager
D.rationale: The decision must be based on the organisational context and the service's needs.

184.question_text: Which statement correctly distinguishes a process from a value stream?
184.explanation: A process transforms inputs into outputs through linked activities. A value stream combines steps, which may mobilise several processes and practices, to create and deliver value to a stakeholder.

A.text: A process transforms inputs into outputs; a value stream links steps to create and deliver value
A.rationale: This distinction separates the operational mechanism from the end-to-end value perspective.

B.text: A process is always external, while a value stream is always internal
B.rationale: Both can cross organisational boundaries.

C.text: A value stream can use only a single process
C.rationale: A value stream can combine several processes, practices, and activities.

D.text: A process must always directly produce a result for an external customer
D.rationale: Some processes support enabling streams without directly delivering external value.

185.scenario: A government announces a national priority favouring digital sovereignty, without a new legal obligation yet in force.
185.question_text: Which PESTLE factor is mainly illustrated?
185.explanation: A governmental orientation or priority mainly belongs to the political factor. It differs from the legal factor, which concerns laws, regulations, and legally binding obligations.

A.text: Political
A.rationale: The scenario describes a governmental orientation rather than a rule already binding.

B.text: Legal
B.rationale: No law or legally binding obligation is yet in force.

C.text: Technological
C.rationale: Digital sovereignty concerns technology, but the described trigger is a political decision.

D.text: Social
D.rationale: The scenario does not mainly focus on societal behaviours or expectations.

186.scenario: A team receives a specific request to build an application, but interviews reveal that the business problem could be solved without a new piece of software.
186.question_text: Which action best matches the "discover" activity?
186.explanation: Discover seeks to understand context, needs, opportunities, risks, and assumptions before committing to a solution. This prevents mistaking a solution request for the real need.

A.text: Validate the problem, stakeholders, and desired outcomes before choosing the solution
A.rationale: This action reduces uncertainty and matches the purpose of discovery.

B.text: Immediately start building the requested application
B.rationale: That decision commits to a solution before the real need has been validated.

C.text: Directly prepare the production release plan
C.rationale: Transition happens after design and implementation of a suitable solution.

D.text: Transfer the request to support
D.rationale: The scenario does not describe an interruption or usage difficulty to resolve.

187.scenario: A design team focuses only on the visible features and ignores the support model, the suppliers, the data, and the skills required.
187.question_text: Which correction best fits the "design" activity?
187.explanation: Design must consider the product or service as a whole, across the four dimensions and the lifecycle. A functional interface is not enough if operation, support, and the required capabilities are not designed.

A.text: Extend the design to the four dimensions as well as operational and support needs
A.rationale: Holistic design prepares a viable solution across its whole lifecycle.

B.text: Defer all these decisions until the first incident
B.rationale: Operational and support capabilities must be anticipated before going live.

C.text: Limit the design to the functional specification
C.rationale: This approach ignores elements essential to durable service provision.

D.text: Assume that suppliers will automatically adapt their services
D.rationale: Supplier dependencies and responsibilities must be explicitly designed and agreed.

188.scenario: A product has passed its technical tests, but users are not trained, data has not been migrated, and support has no procedure.
188.question_text: Which activity should mainly coordinate preparation before operational use?
188.explanation: Transition aims to smoothly introduce new or changed products and services into their usage environment. Preparation includes people, data, support, communications, and technical changes.

A.text: Transition
A.rationale: The gaps described directly concern the state of readiness for moving into operational use.

B.text: Build
B.rationale: The technical solution is already implemented and tested; the problem is about introducing it into service.

C.text: Discover
C.rationale: Needs have already been turned into a product; it is no longer about understanding the initial opportunity.

D.text: Operate
D.rationale: Operation starts when the product is in ongoing running.

189.scenario: A team runs scheduled backups, monitors capacity, handles events, and keeps components in operational condition on a daily basis.
189.question_text: Why do these tasks mainly belong to the "operate" activity rather than to "support"?
189.explanation: Operate covers the running, monitoring, and routine upkeep of products and services. Support mainly steps in to resolve interruptions, difficulties, or assistance needs.

A.text: They routinely maintain the running and performance of systems
A.rationale: The planned, recurring nature of the tasks matches operation.

B.text: They are all triggered by a user incident
B.rationale: The scenario describes routine tasks and not a response to an interruption.

C.text: They prepare a product that is not yet in use
C.rationale: That would rather belong to transition.

D.text: They define the needs of a future service
D.rationale: That activity belongs to discovery and design.

190.question_text: Which statement about the organisation of the eight lifecycle activities is correct?
190.explanation: Lifecycle activities are types of work that are interconnected, not mandatory departments. A single team can contribute to several activities and several activities can run in parallel.

A.text: They do not necessarily correspond to eight distinct teams or departments
A.rationale: ITIL describes activities that can be adapted to the organisation's operating model.

B.text: Each activity must have a legally separate organisation
B.rationale: No legal separation is prescribed by the model.

C.text: A person can participate in only one activity
C.rationale: Responsibilities can span several activities depending on skills and the value stream.

D.text: The activities must always be executed one after another without overlap
D.rationale: The lifecycle is interconnected, iterative, and often non-linear.

191.question_text: Which elements are respectively the main inputs and the output of the ITIL Service Value System?
191.explanation: The Service Value System transforms opportunity and demand into value through its components and activities. Value is not a guaranteed input: it is co-created by the system's operation.

A.text: Opportunity and demand are inputs; value is the output
A.rationale: This relationship describes the overall operation of the ITIL Service Value System.

B.text: Value and outcomes are inputs; practices are the output
B.rationale: Practices are enabling components, while value is the desired output.

C.text: Incidents are the inputs; changes are the output
C.rationale: These elements can appear in some flows but do not define the overall system.

D.text: Governance is the input; the SLA is the output
D.rationale: Governance is a component of the system, and an SLA is not its overall output.

192.scenario: An organisation applies the guiding principles separately from its governance, practices, and value chain.
192.question_text: Which risk does this approach mainly create?
192.explanation: The Service Value System's components are designed to work together. Isolating them can cause inconsistent decisions and prevent the effective transformation of opportunity and demand into value.

A.text: Fragmentation that prevents the components from supporting value creation together
A.rationale: The Service Value System depends on the interactions between its components.

B.text: An automatic increase in availability
B.rationale: Isolating the components does not guarantee any operational improvement.

C.text: The conversion of practices into lifecycle activities
C.rationale: Practices and activities remain distinct concepts even when they interact.

D.text: The removal of any need for governance
D.rationale: Governance remains essential to evaluate, direct, and monitor.

193.question_text: Which statement about the use of the ITIL guiding principles is correct?
193.explanation: The guiding principles are universal recommendations that must be considered in every circumstance. Their application still has to be adapted to context and does not constitute a rigid procedure.

A.text: They are relevant in every circumstance, but their application must be adapted to context
A.rationale: The principles guide decisions without imposing a single procedure.

B.text: Each principle can only be used in a specific lifecycle phase
B.rationale: The principles can apply to every activity and decision.

C.text: A single principle should be chosen for each initiative
C.rationale: Several principles must generally be considered together.

D.text: They replace the organisation's policies and governance
D.rationale: They orient decisions but do not replace governance mechanisms.

194.scenario: An improvement reduces internal processing time but forces customers to provide more information and increases their overall effort.
194.question_text: Which analysis best applies the "focus on value" principle?
194.explanation: Value must be considered from the perspective of consumers and other stakeholders, including experience and indirect effects. An internal optimisation can destroy value if it shifts the effort to the customer.

A.text: Evaluate the total effect on the customer's outcomes and experience, not just the internal gain
A.rationale: The principle requires linking every activity to the value actually perceived.

B.text: Keep the improvement because internal time has decreased
B.rationale: The local gain may be cancelled out by the extra effort imposed on the customer.

C.text: Measure only the number of steps removed
C.rationale: The simplicity of the internal process does not prove value creation.

D.text: Transfer responsibility for value to the sponsor
D.rationale: Value is co-created and must guide decisions of every concerned party.

195.scenario: Members of a team know their process so well that they no longer notice certain workarounds and unnecessary waits.
195.question_text: Which action is particularly useful under the "start where you are" principle?
195.explanation: A person unfamiliar with the service can observe without the preconceptions of teams used to the current way of working. This perspective complements the specialists' data and experience.

A.text: Have the work observed by a person with little prior knowledge of the service
A.rationale: A fresh eye can reveal practices that have become invisible to people used to them.

B.text: Exclude anyone who does not already know the process
B.rationale: This approach deprives the team of a useful independent perspective.

C.text: Replace the process before observing it
C.rationale: The principle recommends assessing what exists before deciding what to change.

D.text: Rely only on official documentation
D.rationale: Documentation can differ from the work actually performed.

196.scenario: A monitoring tool detects a degradation before any user reports it.
196.question_text: Which statement about recording this situation is correct?
196.explanation: An incident can be detected and reported by a user, a technical team, a supplier, or a monitoring tool. The source of the report does not change the need to log and manage it as an incident when an interruption or degradation is present.

A.text: The incident can be recorded even if it was detected automatically
A.rationale: Automatic detection is a valid source for reporting an incident.

B.text: Only users can report an incident
B.rationale: Incidents can be detected by several people or technologies.

C.text: Every monitoring signal must be logged as a problem
C.rationale: A problem is a cause or potential cause, not every detected degradation.

D.text: The situation should only be recorded after a complaint is received
D.rationale: Waiting for a complaint would delay restoration while the degradation is already known.

197.scenario: A manager invites every person in the company to every meeting to demonstrate maximum collaboration.
197.question_text: Which correction best fits the guiding principle?
197.explanation: Effective collaboration involves the right people, at the right time, and at the appropriate level. It means neither universal participation nor a mandatory pursuit of full consensus.

A.text: Involve relevant stakeholders based on the decision and the knowledge required
A.rationale: Collaboration must be targeted to produce better decisions without overload.

B.text: Keep every participant, even when they do not contribute
B.rationale: Excessive participation can slow down work and reduce the quality of exchanges.

C.text: Limit every decision to a single person
C.rationale: This approach risks excluding essential knowledge and perspectives.

D.text: Require unanimity before any action
D.rationale: Collaboration does not always require full consensus.

198.scenario: A team publishes all its raw data to the whole organisation, but decision-makers cannot identify the relevant information.
198.question_text: How should visibility be improved according to ITIL?
198.explanation: Visibility must give stakeholders the relevant, understandable, and timely information they need. Making everything visible without context can create noise rather than support decisions.

A.text: Present stakeholders with the relevant information in a format suitable for their decisions
A.rationale: Useful visibility depends on the audience, need, and context.

B.text: Keep publishing every piece of data without explanation
B.rationale: A maximum volume of data does not guarantee sufficient understanding.

C.text: Hide every difficulty until it is resolved
C.rationale: This approach prevents stakeholders from understanding risks and acting.

D.text: Replace the data with unverified opinions
D.rationale: Visibility must remain grounded in reliable information.

199.scenario: An analysis reveals a weakness in a software component that could cause interruptions, but no complete diagnosis of the associated problem has yet been documented.
199.question_text: Which term best describes the identified weakness?
199.explanation: An error is a fault or vulnerability likely to cause incidents. A known error corresponds to a problem that has already been analysed but not yet resolved.

A.text: An error
A.rationale: The technical weakness likely to cause incidents corresponds to an error.

B.text: A known error
B.rationale: This term assumes that a problem has already been analysed and remains unresolved.

C.text: A service request
C.rationale: No predefined user request is described.

D.text: A service level
D.rationale: A service level is a set of quality metrics.

200.scenario: A process has few steps, but each step requires several validations with no effect on risk or value.
200.question_text: Which conclusion best fits the "keep it simple and practical" principle?
200.explanation: Simplicity is not measured only by the number of steps. Every activity, control, or piece of information should have an identifiable contribution to value, risk, or a necessary outcome.

A.text: Examine and remove validations that contribute to no necessary outcome
A.rationale: The principle recommends the minimum elements required to achieve the objective.

B.text: Keep every validation because the process already has few steps
B.rationale: A step can remain useless or excessively complex even in a short process.

C.text: Add validations to make the process more complete
C.rationale: Additional complexity must be justified by a real contribution.

D.text: Automate the validations before evaluating their usefulness
D.rationale: Automating a useless activity preserves the waste.

201.scenario: An organisation automates the response to every request, including those requiring empathy, judgement, and handling of sensitive exceptions.
201.question_text: Which approach best fits the "optimize and automate" principle?
201.explanation: Automation should be used where it improves value, consistency, and efficiency. Human interventions should be kept when they bring judgement, creativity, or a relationship that automation does not adequately provide.

A.text: Automate repetitive tasks and preserve human intervention when it brings specific value
A.rationale: Automation should support optimised work rather than indiscriminately remove people.

B.text: Automate every activity as soon as it is technically possible
B.rationale: Technical feasibility does not prove that automation improves value or reduces risk.

C.text: Avoid any automation to protect user experience
C.rationale: Well-designed automation can improve speed and consistency.

D.text: Replace value criteria with a headcount-reduction objective
D.rationale: The principle aims at optimising value and outcomes, not a single staffing objective.

202.scenario: The governing body analyses current performance, stakeholder needs, and changes in the external environment.
202.question_text: Which governance activity does this mainly correspond to?
202.explanation: Evaluate consists of examining the organisation, its environment, its options, and stakeholder needs. This activity provides the understanding needed before setting direction.

A.text: Evaluate
A.rationale: Analysing the context, performance, and needs corresponds to evaluation.

B.text: Direct
B.rationale: Direct consists of setting orientation, priorities, and policies.

C.text: Monitor
C.rationale: Monitor mainly checks execution and compliance with the direction given.

D.text: Build
D.rationale: Build is a lifecycle activity, not a governance activity.

203.scenario: After reviewing several options, the board sets investment priorities, approves a risk policy, and communicates the direction to management.
203.question_text: Which governance activity does this mainly correspond to?
203.explanation: Direct consists of assigning the orientation, policies, and priorities that guide the organisation's management. This activity generally follows the evaluation of context and options.

A.text: Direct
A.rationale: Setting priorities and policies corresponds to the direct activity.

B.text: Evaluate
B.rationale: Evaluation analyses the options; the scenario describes the decision and direction chosen.

C.text: Monitor
C.rationale: Monitoring checks results and compliance after execution.

D.text: Discover
D.rationale: Discover concerns product or service needs and opportunities, not the governance direction.

204.scenario: A board delegates the decision on certain digital investments to a committee.
204.question_text: Which statement about governance responsibility is the most correct?
204.explanation: Decision-making authority can be delegated, but the governing body remains accountable for how that authority is exercised and for the outcomes of governance.

A.text: Authority can be delegated, but the ultimate governance accountability remains
A.rationale: Delegation does not remove the obligation of oversight and accountability.

B.text: Delegation permanently transfers every responsibility to the committee
B.rationale: The governing body keeps the ultimate accountability for governance.

C.text: No governance decision can ever be delegated
C.rationale: Framed delegation is possible when it is clearly defined and supervised.

D.text: The committee automatically becomes the service provider
D.rationale: Delegated authority does not change the roles in a service relationship.

205.scenario: An innovation stream uses the "engage" activity twice and runs some tasks of "design" and "obtain or build" in parallel.
205.question_text: Why can this use be correct?
205.explanation: Value chain activities can be used several times, in different orders, and sometimes in parallel within a value stream. The model does not impose a single sequence.

A.text: Value chain activities can be combined and repeated to suit the value stream
A.rationale: The value chain is flexible and adapts to the work needed to create value.

B.text: Each activity can appear only once per product
B.rationale: A stream can return to an activity when new information or decisions are needed.

C.text: Activities must always follow a fixed order
C.rationale: ITIL does not prescribe a universal sequence.

D.text: Parallel tasks are forbidden in a value stream
D.rationale: Several activities can overlap when it is appropriate and controlled.

206.question_text: What lets an organisation consistently execute its digital product and service management activities?
206.explanation: Management practices bring together the organisational resources needed to perform work or achieve an objective. They contribute to lifecycle activities, the value chain, and value streams.

A.text: The management practices
A.rationale: Practices provide the organisational capabilities that let the work be performed.

B.text: The service levels
B.rationale: Service levels define quality metrics but are not the execution capabilities.

C.text: The PESTLE factors
C.rationale: PESTLE describes external influences and not the organisation's management resources.

D.text: The service offerings
D.rationale: Offerings describe what is proposed to consumers, not the full set of internal capabilities.

207.question_text: Which statement best distinguishes general management practices from product and service management practices?
207.explanation: General practices support capabilities applicable across the whole organisation. Product and service management practices focus more directly on creating, delivering, operating, and improving those products and services.

A.text: General practices support the organisation broadly; the others are directly oriented towards products and services
A.rationale: The distinction mainly relies on the scope and purpose of the capabilities.

B.text: General practices are mandatory, while the others are optional
B.rationale: ITIL requires adapting every practice to context, without this mandatory/optional classification.

C.text: General practices are always in-house and the others always outsourced
C.rationale: Both groups can mobilise internal and external resources.

D.text: General practices never contribute to value streams
D.rationale: They can be essential to many flows and activities.

208.scenario: An organisation wants to clarify the roles, skills, team structures, and communication needs required for a practice.
208.question_text: Which part of the practice guide should it mainly consult?
208.explanation: The "organizations and people" chapter examines the roles, responsibilities, skills, structures, culture, and communication needed for the practice's success.

A.text: Organizations and people
A.rationale: This part directly addresses the practice's human and organisational capabilities.

B.text: Information and technology
B.rationale: This part mainly addresses information, tools, and automation possibilities.

C.text: Partners and suppliers
C.rationale: This part examines contributions and relationships with third parties.

D.text: Value streams and processes
D.rationale: This part describes the integration of the practice into value streams and its work processes.

209.scenario: An organisation knows its vision and has established a baseline for current performance.
209.question_text: What must it mainly define at the "Where do we want to be?" step?
209.explanation: This step translates the vision into measurable objectives and improvement targets. It clarifies the gap to close without yet detailing the implementation actions in full.

A.text: Measurable objectives and targets describing the desired future state
A.rationale: The step defines the concrete destination based on the vision and current state.

B.text: A detailed list of actions already executed
B.rationale: Execution belongs to the "act" step and comes after planning.

C.text: Only a new baseline measure of the current state
C.rationale: The baseline was already established at the previous step.

D.text: The method for keeping momentum going after success
D.rationale: Keeping momentum going is handled at the last step of the model.

210.scenario: A team has defined the vision, the current state, and the desired targets.
210.question_text: What is the main objective of the "How do we get there?" step?
210.explanation: This step selects and organises the initiatives needed to move from the current state to the target state. It includes defining a realistic plan, priorities, resources, and control measures.

A.text: Develop an improvement approach and plan to reach the targets
A.rationale: The plan links the identified gap to the actions that will close it.

B.text: Immediately declare the improvement successful
B.rationale: Success must be verified after implementation and after measuring the results.

C.text: Redefine the existence of the organisation
C.rationale: The vision and context guide the plan, but this step does not aim to redefine the organisation.

D.text: Replace every existing practice
D.rationale: The plan must be proportionate and can reuse capabilities that are already effective.

211.scenario: A map shows 20 minutes of actual processing and three days of waiting between two teams.
211.question_text: What does this comparison mainly highlight?
211.explanation: A value stream map distinguishes, among other things, processing time from waiting time. This distinction lets you identify delays that do not directly add value.

A.text: Most of the delay comes from waiting rather than actual work
A.rationale: The map reveals a significant interruption of flow between steps.

B.text: The actual processing must necessarily be automated
B.rationale: Automation is not automatically the best response to a waiting delay.

C.text: The three days constitute a process output
C.rationale: Waiting is a delay in the flow, not a produced deliverable.

D.text: The stream is core because it lasts more than three days
D.rationale: The core / enabling classification depends on the value delivered, not on duration.

212.scenario: A stream directly delivers a registration request to an external customer. A second stream recruits and trains the employees needed for the first.
212.question_text: Which criterion mainly determines their classification?
212.explanation: A core stream directly delivers value to a customer or another external stakeholder. An enabling stream provides the capabilities or resources needed by one or more core streams.

A.text: The stream's direct or indirect link to the value delivered to the external stakeholder
A.rationale: The first is core and the second enabling because of their respective contribution to external value.

B.text: The number of employees participating in each stream
B.rationale: Team size does not determine the nature of the stream.

C.text: Whether or not the stream uses technology
C.rationale: Both types of stream can be heavily or lightly technological.

D.text: The total duration of the stream
D.rationale: Duration influences performance but not the core / enabling classification.

213.scenario: Every team meets its local objectives, but queues and rework increase between teams.
213.question_text: Which value stream management objective is the most relevant?
213.explanation: Value stream management aims to optimise end-to-end flow and overall value. It reduces local optimisations that push problems to another step.

A.text: Improve end-to-end flow rather than maximise every step separately
A.rationale: This approach tackles queues, handoffs, and rework at the system level.

B.text: Raise local targets without changing the interactions
B.rationale: Stricter local targets can worsen imbalances in the flow.

C.text: Only measure the productivity of the slowest team
C.rationale: A single team does not represent every cause of delay and rework.

D.text: Drop the mapping as soon as every team hits its target
D.rationale: Local performance does not prove that the overall flow efficiently creates value.

214.scenario: One tool produces a summary from existing documents. Another tool plans a series of actions, calls several systems, and adapts its plan based on the results obtained.
214.explanation: Generative AI produces new content from models and instructions. Agentic AI pursues a goal by planning and executing actions with a degree of autonomy that must be framed by appropriate governance.

A.text: The first illustrates generative AI; the second illustrates agentic AI
A.rationale: Content generation is distinct from autonomously planning and executing actions.

B.text: The first illustrates agentic AI; the second is a simple knowledge base
B.rationale: The ability to adapt and execute a plan is more characteristic of agentic AI.

C.text: Both tools are purely deterministic automations
C.rationale: The scenario describes generation and adaptation capabilities that go beyond a fully predefined sequence.

D.text: Neither tool requires governance
D.rationale: AI uses must be framed according to their risks, data, and level of autonomy.

215.scenario: An organisation uses DevOps to bring development and operations closer together, automate deployments, and speed up feedback. It wants to keep consistent management of value, risk, and the lifecycle.
215.question_text: How does ITIL best complement DevOps?
215.explanation: DevOps brings practices of collaboration, fast flow, and automation. ITIL provides an adaptable framework linking those practices to value, governance, service relationships, and the full lifecycle.

A.text: ITIL links DevOps practices to value, governance, and end-to-end product and service management
A.rationale: The two approaches are complementary and can be adapted to the same operating model.

B.text: ITIL requires replacing DevOps practices with sequential processes
B.rationale: ITIL is adaptable and does not prescribe dropping DevOps practices.

C.text: DevOps makes governance and risk management unnecessary
C.rationale: Speed and automation still require proportionate direction and controls.

D.text: ITIL applies only after go-live
D.rationale: ITIL covers the whole lifecycle, from discovery to support.

216.scenario: A portal is technically available and meets its response times, but users frequently abandon their journeys because the path is confusing across the website, the mobile app, and the emails received.
216.question_text: Which aspect must be evaluated as a priority to understand this situation?
216.explanation: The digital experience covers the perceptions and interactions produced by all digital touchpoints. Good technical performance in isolation does not guarantee a consistent experience across the whole journey.

A.text: The consistency of the digital experience across the various touchpoints
A.rationale: The abandonments appear linked to the overall digital journey rather than the availability of a single component.

B.text: Only the monthly availability of the portal
B.rationale: Availability is being met and does not measure the clarity or continuity of the journey.

C.text: Only the number of releases put into production
C.rationale: Release volume does not demonstrate that digital interactions are consistent.

D.text: Only the hosting cost of the application
D.rationale: The provider's cost does not directly explain the difficulties users experience.

217.scenario: A bank's mobile app is easy to use, but the customer then receives contradictory information from the call centre and the branch.
217.question_text: Which conclusion correctly distinguishes user experience from customer experience?
217.explanation: User experience mainly concerns interaction with a product or interface. Customer experience is broader and encompasses all the customer's interactions with the organisation.

A.text: The app's UX can be good while the overall CX remains poor
A.rationale: A satisfying interface does not necessarily compensate for inconsistencies encountered in other interactions.

B.text: A good UX automatically guarantees a good CX
B.rationale: CX covers more touchpoints than app usage.

C.text: CX concerns only internal users
C.rationale: CX describes a customer's overall experience with an organisation.

D.text: UX corresponds only to meeting service levels
D.rationale: UX notably includes usability and the user's perceptions and reactions.

218.scenario: A digital assistant generally provides accurate answers, but it never specifies which data it uses or how to contest an incorrect decision.
218.question_text: Which experience factor is mainly at risk of being weakened?
218.explanation: Trust depends notably on transparency, perceived reliability, protection of stakeholder interests, and the ability to obtain redress. High performance is not enough if operation appears uncontrollable.

A.text: Stakeholder trust
A.rationale: The lack of transparency and recourse can reduce willingness to rely on the system.

B.text: The infrastructure's technical capacity
B.rationale: The scenario describes no resource or capacity shortfall.

C.text: Goods transfer
C.rationale: No resource ownership is transferred to the consumer.

D.text: The value stream classification
D.rationale: The difficulty concerns the perception and governance of the assistant, not the stream type.

219.scenario: A team defines a new procedure only from the constraints of the existing system, without observing users or testing prototypes with them.
219.question_text: Which approach should be added as a priority?
219.explanation: Human-centred design starts with understanding people, their goals, and their context. It uses repeated participation and feedback to design a usable and relevant solution.

A.text: Involve users in research, prototyping, and iterative testing
A.rationale: This approach grounds design in the actual needs and behaviours of the people concerned.

B.text: Finalise the entire solution before showing it to users
B.rationale: Late feedback makes design errors harder and more expensive to fix.

C.text: Replace observations with the technical team's preferences
C.rationale: Internal assumptions are not evidence about real experience.

D.text: Measure only server uptime
D.rationale: This technical measure does not inform about usability or fit to human needs.

220.scenario: A service meets a 99.9% availability SLA, but users report that it is difficult to complete their tasks and that they do not trust it.
220.question_text: Which mechanism would best complement the SLA?
220.explanation: An experience level agreement (XLA) focuses on the outcomes and perceptions experienced by users. It complements the operational metrics of an SLA without necessarily replacing them.

A.text: An XLA measuring the experience and outcomes perceived by users
A.rationale: The problem concerns an unsatisfactory experience despite meeting the technical metrics.

B.text: An SLA containing only a higher availability target
B.rationale: An additional technical target does not necessarily measure ease of use or trust.

C.text: A more detailed inventory of IT assets
C.rationale: Knowledge of assets does not directly represent the experience felt.

D.text: An increase in the number of closed requests
D.rationale: Closure volume can rise without improving user outcomes.

221.question_text: Which statement best describes a strategy?
221.explanation: A strategy provides a high-level approach for progressing towards long-term objectives in a given context. It orients choices and resource allocation without detailing every operational action.

A.text: A high-level approach aimed at achieving long-term objectives
A.rationale: Strategy provides consistent direction for decisions and resource use.

B.text: An exhaustive list of every employee's daily tasks
B.rationale: This description matches operational plans or procedures more than strategy.

C.text: A single measure used to evaluate a service
C.rationale: A measure may track strategy implementation but does not constitute the strategy.

D.text: An improvised reaction to every event encountered
D.rationale: A strategy creates coherent orientation rather than a sequence of isolated reactions.

222.scenario: A company wants to grow its market share among small businesses. It decides to use a self-service platform, data analytics, and AI to offer personalised services.
222.question_text: Which distinction is the most correct?
222.explanation: Business strategy defines the objectives and choices that enable the organisation to succeed. Digital strategy specifies how digital capabilities, technologies, and data will contribute to those objectives.

A.text: Growing market share belongs to business strategy, while using the platform, data, and AI belongs to digital strategy
A.rationale: Digital strategy here supports a business objective defined by business strategy.

B.text: Digital strategy fully replaces business strategy
B.rationale: Digital choices must remain aligned with the organisation's overall objectives.

C.text: Business strategy only describes the technical architecture
C.rationale: Technical architecture belongs mainly to the implementation of digital choices.

D.text: The two strategies must be developed without interaction
D.rationale: A lack of alignment can produce digital investments that do not contribute to business results.

223.question_text: Which statement best represents an organisation's mission?
223.explanation: The mission describes what the organisation currently does and its reason for existing in the present. It differs from the vision, which describes a desired future state.

A.text: We currently provide accessible financial services to small businesses
A.rationale: The statement describes current activity and the organisation's present function.

B.text: Become Europe's most trusted digital financial provider within five years
B.rationale: This statement describes a future aspiration and matches a vision.

C.text: Increase revenue by 8% next quarter
C.rationale: This is a measurable target rather than a mission statement.

D.text: Deploy the new application before September
D.rationale: This proposition describes a short-term implementation objective.

224.question_text: Which proposition mainly constitutes a vision?
224.explanation: A vision describes the ambitious future state the organisation wants to reach. It provides inspiring direction without being a detailed plan.

A.text: Be recognised as the organisation that makes digital public services accessible to everyone
A.rationale: The proposition expresses an aspiration about the organisation's future identity.

B.text: Currently operate an online public services platform
B.rationale: This statement describes present activity and matches a mission more than a vision.

C.text: Reduce average response time by ten seconds
C.rationale: This is a precise operational target rather than an inspiring future state.

D.text: Hold the governance meeting every month
D.rationale: This proposition describes a recurring activity and not a future direction.

225.question_text: Which statement best describes an organisation's purpose?
225.explanation: Purpose expresses what the organisation brings to its consumers and other stakeholders, as well as the fundamental reason for that contribution. It helps link choices to more lasting value.

A.text: What the organisation brings to its stakeholders and why that contribution matters
A.rationale: Purpose explains the fundamental contribution and its significance.

B.text: The detail of every procedure applied today
B.rationale: Procedures explain how the work is done, not why the organisation exists.

C.text: A list of technologies that will be bought
C.rationale: Technologies are means and do not define the organisation's fundamental contribution.

D.text: The result of the latest performance report
D.rationale: A measured result is not a durable statement of purpose.

226.scenario: An organisation faces rapid market changes, results that are hard to predict, many dependencies, and information that can be interpreted in several ways.
226.question_text: Which concept best describes this environment?
226.explanation: VUCA stands for volatility, uncertainty, complexity, and ambiguity. It helps leaders recognise the different forms of difficulty encountered when making strategic decisions.

A.text: A VUCA environment
A.rationale: The scenario combines the four characteristics covered by the acronym.

B.text: An experience level agreement
B.rationale: An XLA measures experience and does not describe the conditions of the strategic environment.

C.text: An enabling value stream
C.rationale: An enabling stream supports value creation but does not define an unstable, complex environment.

D.text: A basic service relationship
D.rationale: The relationship type does not represent the four conditions described.

227.scenario: During a transformation, a leader communicates a clear direction, acknowledges uncertainties, encourages learning, and adapts decisions when new evidence appears.
227.question_text: Why is this behaviour particularly important?
227.explanation: Leadership helps make sense of situations, mobilise people, and create the conditions that enable adaptation. In a complex environment it is not only about imposing fixed instructions.

A.text: It combines direction, mobilisation, and adaptation in the face of uncertainty
A.rationale: These behaviours let teams progress without pretending that all answers are known.

B.text: It transfers every decision responsibility to the teams
B.rationale: Autonomy can be encouraged, but leadership retains a direction-setting responsibility.

C.text: It guarantees that the initial plan will never need to change
C.rationale: Adapting to new evidence is essential in an uncertain environment.

D.text: It replaces the need for governance
D.rationale: Leadership and governance are complementary and fulfil different functions.

228.scenario: A team modifies the form of an application in a single day. Another initiative simultaneously redefines the operating model, skills, culture, and products of the organisation.
228.question_text: Which distinction is the most correct?
228.explanation: A change can be limited to a particular modification. A transformation corresponds to a deeper, coordinated evolution of the organisation, its capabilities, and the way it creates value.

A.text: The first initiative is a limited change; the second is a transformation
A.rationale: The second modifies several fundamental elements of the organisation in an integrated way.

B.text: Any technical modification automatically constitutes a transformation
B.rationale: The scope and depth of the evolution distinguish a transformation from an isolated change.

C.text: A transformation concerns only the replacement of technologies
C.rationale: It can also modify people, culture, structures, processes, and business models.

D.text: Change and transformation are strictly synonymous
D.rationale: A transformation generally implies a broader systemic scope.

229.scenario: An organisation has completed the project to deploy a new tool, but behaviours, responsibilities, and decisions remain unchanged and the old workarounds continue.
229.question_text: Why can the transformation not yet be considered successful?
229.explanation: A transformation is not limited to delivering a technology or closing a project. The new capabilities and ways of working must be adopted, embedded, and sustained to produce the desired outcomes durably.

A.text: Because the new ways of working are not yet embedded in real operations
A.rationale: Delivering the tool has not produced the expected durable change in behaviours and capabilities.

B.text: Because any transformation must necessarily last several years
B.rationale: Duration alone is not a success criterion.

C.text: Because a transformation must never use a new tool
C.rationale: Technology can support the transformation, but is not sufficient on its own.

D.text: Because the project did not create enough documentation
D.rationale: Documentation may be useful, but the main issue is the lack of adoption and embedding.

230.scenario: After a transformation initiative, the new responsibilities and methods are transferred to the permanent teams, who must use and improve them in their daily work.
230.explanation: A transformation produces changes that must ultimately be embedded in ongoing activities, or business as usual. This embedding lets the benefits be sustained after the temporary initiative ends.

A.text: The transition from transformation to business as usual
A.rationale: Permanent teams take over the new capabilities in daily operation.

B.text: The transition from operation to discovery
B.rationale: The scenario concerns the durable embedding of a change and not the exploration of a new opportunity.

C.text: Replacing governance with operational management
C.rationale: Governance continues to direct and monitor even after operational embedding.

D.text: The conversion of a service into a good
D.rationale: No ownership transfer is described.

231.scenario: A digital strategy plans for a personalised experience, but the approved investments only concern reducing infrastructure costs.
231.question_text: Which problem must be corrected as a priority?
231.explanation: Implementing a strategy requires aligning investments, initiatives, and decisions with the desired strategic outcomes. A strategy not reflected in resource allocation remains essentially declarative.

A.text: The lack of alignment between investments and strategic outcomes
A.rationale: The approved resources do not directly support the announced personalisation.

B.text: The absence of a sufficient number of guiding principles
B.rationale: The principles exist independently of this allocation inconsistency.

C.text: The fact that the strategy contains an experience objective
C.rationale: Experience can legitimately be a strategic outcome.

D.text: The use of a digital strategy alongside a business strategy
D.rationale: This complementarity is appropriate when both strategies are aligned.

232.scenario: A team uses an AI model to automate the classification of requests, but no rule defines the allowed decisions, the acceptable risks, or the responsibilities.
232.explanation: Using AI consists of applying its capabilities to work. Governing AI consists of evaluating, directing, and monitoring its use so that it remains responsible, compliant, and aligned with objectives.

A.text: AI governance defining direction, controls, and responsibilities
A.rationale: The problem is about the direction and control of use, not about a missing feature.

B.text: An additional content generation capability
B.rationale: The model already performs the expected work; the gaps concern its oversight.

C.text: An automatic increase in the number of decisions made
C.rationale: Increasing usage without governance would potentially amplify the risks.

D.text: The removal of any human intervention
D.rationale: Responsible governance may on the contrary require human oversight.

233.scenario: An AI automatically refuses certain access requests. Neither users nor managers can understand the factors that influenced the refusals.
233.question_text: Which governance principle must be reinforced as a priority?
233.explanation: Transparency makes the use, data, and functioning of an AI system sufficiently understandable. It supports contestability, oversight, and accountability of decisions.

A.text: Transparency of decisions and their main factors
A.rationale: Stakeholders must have sufficient information to understand and review the refusals.

B.text: Increasing the volume of automated decisions
B.rationale: Higher usage does not solve the absence of explanations.

C.text: Removing activity logs
C.rationale: Removing traces would further reduce the ability to control the system.

D.text: Transferring ownership of the model to users
D.rationale: Ownership is not necessary to provide appropriate transparency.

234.scenario: When an AI system produces a harmful decision, the business team claims the vendor is responsible, while the vendor claims the model decided by itself.
234.question_text: Which measure best matches responsible governance?
234.explanation: The organisation must clearly assign responsibility for decisions, oversight, and responses to AI-related incidents. An automated system cannot itself bear organisational accountability.

A.text: Define human owners accountable for decisions, controls, and consequences
A.rationale: Explicit accountability prevents an automated decision from becoming an accountability gap.

B.text: Consider the model as solely responsible for its decisions
B.rationale: A model cannot bear organisational or legal accountability.

C.text: Avoid documenting responsibilities to preserve flexibility
C.rationale: Ambiguous responsibilities increase risks and slow down response.

D.text: Automatically assign every responsibility to the end user
D.rationale: The user does not necessarily control the system's design, data, and rules.

235.scenario: An AI recommends automatically suspending a critical service when it detects an anomaly, but some false positives could cause a significant outage.
235.question_text: Which control is the most appropriate?
235.explanation: Human oversight must be proportionate to the possible consequences and to the system's uncertainty. High-impact decisions may require validation or the possibility of human intervention.

A.text: Require human validation before high-impact suspensions
A.rationale: The control preserves the benefits of automated detection while reducing the risk of harmful decisions.

B.text: Allow every suspension without any possibility of intervention
B.rationale: False positives could then automatically cause major consequences.

C.text: Prohibit any use of AI to detect anomalies
C.rationale: Proportionate oversight may be preferable to abandoning the capability entirely.

D.text: Ask users to restore the service themselves
D.rationale: This action transfers the risk without controlling the initial decision.

236.scenario: An incident prediction model is trained with incomplete, outdated data containing unnecessary personal information.
236.question_text: Which action should be prioritised before extending its use?
236.explanation: The quality of AI outputs strongly depends on suitable, accurate, and representative data. Governance must also limit personal data to what is necessary and protect it properly.

A.text: Improve data quality and apply confidentiality and minimisation requirements
A.rationale: This action addresses both the model's reliability and the risks related to personal data.

B.text: Add more data without checking its relevance
B.rationale: Greater volume can amplify quality defects and privacy risks.

C.text: Only hide the model's name in the interface
C.rationale: This measure corrects neither the inadequate data nor its excessive use.

D.text: Deploy the model and evaluate the data after several incidents
D.rationale: Risks must be addressed before extended and potentially harmful use.

237.question_text: What is the main purpose of the "6C" AI capability model?
237.explanation: The 6C model classifies AI capabilities into creation, curation, clarification, cognition, communication, and coordination. This classification helps understand possible uses and associate each capability with relevant risks and controls.

A.text: Classify AI capabilities to analyse uses, risks, and controls
A.rationale: The model provides a structured vocabulary for examining what AI can do.

B.text: Entirely replace the ITIL Service Value System
B.rationale: The model complements ITIL and does not replace its fundamental components.

C.text: Define six mandatory levels of organisational maturity
C.rationale: The six items are capability categories, not sequential levels.

D.text: Guarantee that an AI system is automatically compliant
D.rationale: The classification supports analysis but does not constitute a compliance guarantee.

238.scenario: An organisation identifies that a system has creation and communication capabilities, and then concludes that no other control is needed.
238.explanation: The capability model describes what AI can do. Governance determines how its use must be evaluated, directed, and monitored based on risks and objectives.

A.text: Identifying capabilities does not replace defining responsibilities, risks, and controls
A.rationale: The capability model and governance answer two different but complementary questions.

B.text: Creation and communication capabilities can never be governed
B.rationale: Any capability may require controls adapted to its context and impact.

C.text: Governance only serves to select the model's supplier
C.rationale: It more broadly covers direction, oversight, risk, and accountability.

D.text: The 6C model is already a service level agreement
D.rationale: It classifies AI capabilities and does not define agreed quality metrics.

239.scenario: An organisation wants to measure the success of the "discover" activity before authorising the detailed design of a new product.
239.question_text: Which indicator would provide the most relevant evidence?
239.explanation: Discovery must improve understanding of needs, opportunities, constraints, and assumptions. Success is shown notably by the validation of problems and the reduction of uncertainty before investment.

A.text: The proportion of critical assumptions validated with stakeholders
A.rationale: This measure indicates that the team is reducing uncertainty about the need and the opportunity.

B.text: The number of lines of code already produced
B.rationale: Building the solution is not the main objective of discovery.

C.text: The number of incidents resolved in production
C.rationale: This measure mainly concerns products already in operation.

D.text: The percentage of user accounts activated
D.rationale: User activation belongs more to service delivery.

240.scenario: A team must choose a primary indicator to evaluate the design quality of a future service.
240.question_text: Which indicator is the most complete according to ITIL?
240.explanation: Design must prepare a product or service satisfying the expected utility, warranty, experience, and sustainability. A measure limited to functionality therefore does not cover the whole designed quality.

A.text: The percentage of validated requirements covering utility, warranty, experience, and sustainability
A.rationale: This indicator verifies that the four essential aspects have been incorporated in the design.

B.text: The total number of screens designed
B.rationale: Screen count does not demonstrate the service's overall fit.

C.text: The number of developers assigned to the project
C.rationale: Team size does not measure design quality.

D.text: The amount of storage already acquired
D.rationale: This measure concerns a specific resource and not the complete design.

241.scenario: An organisation has just obtained the resources needed for a new service from several suppliers.
241.question_text: Which indicator best measures the success of the "acquire" activity?
241.explanation: Acquisition must supply the appropriate resources, at the necessary quality level, at the right time, and under the required conditions. Cost alone is insufficient when resources are inadequate or delivered too late.

A.text: The proportion of resources obtained on time and matching the agreed requirements
A.rationale: This measure covers both the availability and the quality of the acquired resources.

B.text: The number of suppliers contacted
B.rationale: A high number of contacts guarantees neither the quality nor the availability of the resources.

C.text: The number of negotiation meetings
C.rationale: Activity performed is not necessarily a successful acquisition outcome.

D.text: The number of defects found after production release
D.rationale: This late measure does not directly concern the resources' compliance at the time of acquisition.

242.scenario: A team finishes the implementation and integration of the components of a digital product.
242.question_text: Which set of measures best evaluates the success of the "build" activity?
242.explanation: Build must produce integrated components that comply with specifications and pass the necessary tests. Development speed is not enough if the resulting solution is defective or incomplete.

A.text: Compliance with specifications and test pass rate
A.rationale: These measures verify that the built product matches the design and works as expected.

B.text: The number of code changes and the number of developers
B.rationale: These volumes do not demonstrate the product's quality or compliance.

C.text: Supplier satisfaction and licence cost
C.rationale: These items do not directly measure the built solution's quality.

D.text: The number of users registered before the build
D.rationale: This measure says nothing about the technical outcome of the build.

243.scenario: A new release has just been introduced into the operational environment.
243.question_text: Which measure is the most relevant for evaluating the quality of the transition?
243.explanation: A successful transition introduces changes with acceptable impact and without generating an excessive number of errors or interruptions. It also takes into account the readiness of users and teams.

A.text: The number of errors and the business impact attributable to the transition
A.rationale: This measure directly links introducing the change to its operational consequences.

B.text: The number of features considered during discovery
B.rationale: This measure concerns an earlier step and does not demonstrate the quality of the operational move.

C.text: The total number of servers in the organisation
C.rationale: Infrastructure size does not measure the effects of the transition.

D.text: The number of suppliers in the catalogue
D.rationale: This information does not reflect the errors or impacts introduced.

244.scenario: An organisation evaluates the daily performance of the "operate" activity for a critical service.
244.question_text: Which set of indicators is the most relevant?
244.explanation: Operation must keep products and services within the expected conditions. Measures must therefore compare their performance, reliability, and capacity to the agreed levels.

A.text: Availability, reliability, and performance against agreed levels
A.rationale: These indicators show whether the service runs sustainably as expected.

B.text: The number of mock-ups produced during design
B.rationale: Mock-ups do not measure the quality of daily operation.

C.text: The number of candidates interviewed for a position
C.rationale: This recruitment measure does not directly reflect the service's operational performance.

D.text: The number of strategies proposed to the board
D.rationale: This measure concerns strategic thinking and not the operation of the service.

245.scenario: A service is operational and the organisation wants to measure the success of the "deliver" activity.
245.question_text: Which indicator is the most directly relevant?
245.explanation: Deliver covers the provision of the service and normal interactions with users, notably onboarding, planned requests, and access to the service. Measures must therefore reflect meeting commitments and the outcomes of those interactions.

A.text: The proportion of services and requests provided within the agreed levels
A.rationale: This measure indicates whether consumers actually receive the expected items under the agreed conditions.

B.text: The number of technical components developed
B.rationale: This measure mainly concerns building the product.

C.text: The number of assumptions identified during discovery
C.rationale: This measure does not represent ongoing delivery to users.

D.text: The number of policies approved by governance
D.rationale: Policies guide the work, but do not directly measure the quality of delivery.

246.scenario: An organisation wants to measure the ability of the "support" activity to limit the consequences of interruptions.
246.question_text: Which indicator is the most appropriate?
246.explanation: Support notably aims to restore the service quickly and help users facing difficulties. A restoration measure must be complemented by real impact to avoid a purely quantitative reading.

A.text: Service restoration time, considered alongside the impact of interruptions
A.rationale: This indicator directly measures the speed and effectiveness of the support response.

B.text: The number of products described in the strategy
B.rationale: This information does not measure restoration or assistance provided.

C.text: The number of resources purchased from suppliers
C.rationale: This measure mainly concerns acquisition.

D.text: The number of prototypes created before building
D.rationale: Prototyping does not measure the effectiveness of operational support.

247.question_text: Which statement best describes the management of digital products and services?
247.explanation: The management of digital products and services is a set of specialised organisational capabilities that let value be created through digital products and services. It concerns the organisation as a whole and is not limited to a technical team's work.

A.text: A set of specialised organisational capabilities that enable value creation through digital products and services
A.rationale: This proposition reflects the organisational scope and value-creation objective of the concept.

B.text: A method reserved for internal software development
B.rationale: The concept covers the full lifecycle of digital products and services, not just internal development.

C.text: A practice intended only to automate the service desk
C.rationale: Automating support is only one possible use and does not define digital management overall.

D.text: A procedure for transferring every risk to the supplier
D.rationale: Digital management organises value-creation capabilities and does not guarantee full risk transfer.

248.question_text: Which definition best matches a service?
248.explanation: A service enables value co-creation by facilitating outcomes the customer wants without them having to manage certain specific costs and risks. A service can be digital or non-digital.

A.text: A means of enabling value co-creation by facilitating desired outcomes, without the customer managing certain specific costs and risks
A.rationale: This answer covers outcomes, value co-creation, and the taking on of certain costs and risks.

B.text: Any technological resource owned by a provider
B.rationale: A resource can contribute to a service but does not necessarily constitute one.

C.text: A digital product that must be accessible over the internet
C.rationale: A service is not always digital and is not the same as the product that supports it.

D.text: An output delivered to the consumer regardless of the outcomes obtained
D.rationale: A service aims to facilitate outcomes and is not defined only by an output delivered.

249.question_text: Which statement best describes continual improvement as a fundamental concept?
249.explanation: Continual improvement consists of continually aligning products, services, practices, and other management elements with changing needs. It relies on the repeated identification and delivery of improvements at every level.

A.text: A recurring activity aimed at aligning products, services, and practices with changing needs
A.rationale: Continuity and alignment with changing needs are at the heart of the concept.

B.text: An exceptional project executed only when performance becomes critical
B.rationale: Continual improvement is not limited to crises or to a one-off initiative.

C.text: An annual review intended only to reduce costs
C.rationale: It can reduce costs, but more broadly it pursues value, quality, and adaptation.

D.text: The exclusive responsibility of the improvement-specialist team
D.rationale: A team can coordinate the efforts, but improvement must be embedded across the whole organisation.

250.scenario: A provider hands terminals to the customer. After delivery, the customer becomes the owner and takes on their maintenance.
250.question_text: Which term best describes the item transferred in this service interaction?
250.explanation: In ITIL, a good is an item transferred to the consumer along with the associated rights and responsibilities. It differs from access to a resource, which remains under the provider's control.

A.text: A good (transferred item)
A.rationale: Ownership and responsibility pass to the consumer, which characterises the transfer of a good.

B.text: Access to resources
B.rationale: In access to resources, the provider generally keeps control of the resource.

C.text: A service action
C.rationale: A service action is an activity performed for the consumer, not an item whose ownership is transferred.

D.text: A service level
D.rationale: A service level is a set of metrics and not a transferred resource.

251.scenario: A company has product, operations, customer experience, and supplier teams using incompatible methods and vocabularies.
251.question_text: Which ITIL benefit is the most directly relevant for this company?
251.explanation: ITIL provides a common language and a consistent system for aligning products, services, teams, and partners on value. This alignment eases cross-functional decisions and reduces fragmentation.

A.text: Create a common language and align the organisation's capabilities on value
A.rationale: This benefit directly addresses inconsistencies between teams and disciplines.

B.text: Impose an identical organisational structure on every company
B.rationale: ITIL is adaptable and does not prescribe a universal structure.

C.text: Remove the need for governance decisions
C.rationale: ITIL reinforces governance rather than making it unnecessary.

D.text: Automatically replace every existing tool
D.rationale: ITIL guides management and improvement without imposing systematic tool replacement.

252.scenario: A managed service provider must deliver consistent services to several customers while adapting the agreements, risks, and experiences to each context.
252.question_text: Which ITIL benefit best supports this objective?
252.explanation: ITIL helps a managed service provider standardise its capabilities while adapting offerings, relationships, and value streams. It supports more consistent, measurable, and scalable delivery.

A.text: Combine consistent capabilities with adaptation to each customer's needs and relationships
A.rationale: This combination supports scalability without ignoring consumers' specific context.

B.text: Use exactly the same SLA and relationship for every customer
B.rationale: Needs, outcomes, and relationship types can differ across customers.

C.text: Automatically transfer every operational risk to the consumers
C.rationale: Risks must be understood and managed in the relationship, not moved without analysis.

D.text: Only measure the number of hours billed
D.rationale: An effort measure does not demonstrate the quality or value of the services provided.

253.scenario: A vendor produces a strong application, but its partners have difficulty integrating it into services that generate business outcomes.
253.question_text: Which ITIL benefit is the most relevant for this digital product provider?
253.explanation: ITIL helps the digital product provider link the product's capabilities, associated services, value streams, and stakeholder outcomes. Success is therefore not limited to the product's technical quality.

A.text: Link the product's capabilities to services, value streams, and desired outcomes
A.rationale: This approach lets the product genuinely contribute to value creation in its ecosystem.

B.text: Limit the provider's responsibility to delivering the code
B.rationale: Value also depends on integration, use, and associated services.

C.text: Avoid any collaboration with integrators and service providers
C.rationale: Partners often help turn the product's capabilities into outcomes.

D.text: Evaluate success only by the number of features
D.rationale: Feature volume does not prove that the desired outcomes are achieved.

254.scenario: A professional works successively in support, product management, and digital transformation.
254.question_text: Which ITIL benefit is the most useful in this career path?
254.explanation: ITIL provides a common vocabulary and models that transfer across roles related to products, services, strategy, experience, and transformation. This knowledge eases collaboration and professional mobility.

A.text: Concepts and capabilities transferable across several digital management roles
A.rationale: The common framework stays relevant as professional responsibilities evolve.

B.text: A guarantee of automatically obtaining a leadership role
B.rationale: A certification supports skills but does not guarantee promotion.

C.text: A specialisation limited to service desk operation
C.rationale: Version 5 covers a much broader field than operational support.

D.text: A method that replaces every practical experience
D.rationale: The framework complements experience and does not make it unnecessary.

255.question_text: Which statement correctly distinguishes a service interaction from a service relationship?
255.explanation: A service interaction is a reciprocal action between provider and consumer that contributes to value co-creation. A service relationship is broader and encompasses the durable set of provision, consumption, and relationship management.

A.text: An interaction is a particular reciprocal action; a relationship encompasses the durable set of cooperation between parties
A.rationale: This answer correctly distinguishes the specific event or exchange from the overall relational frame.

B.text: A service interaction and a service relationship are strictly synonymous
B.rationale: The relationship has broader scope than each individual interaction.

C.text: An interaction concerns only incidents, while a relationship concerns only contracts
C.rationale: Interactions can take many forms and the relationship goes well beyond the contract alone.

D.text: A service relationship ends after each interaction
D.rationale: A relationship can continue through many successive interactions.

256.scenario: A provider meets its initial assumptions but rarely gathers consumer feedback after go-live.
256.question_text: Why is feedback essential to value co-creation?
256.explanation: Feedback reveals the outcomes, perceptions, and difficulties actually experienced by stakeholders. It lets the provider and consumer jointly adjust the products, services, and behaviours needed for value.

A.text: It lets the parties learn from real experience and adjust their contribution to value
A.rationale: Co-creation thus becomes a learning loop rather than a fixed assumption.

B.text: It automatically transfers responsibility for outcomes to the consumer
B.rationale: Feedback supports shared responsibility and does not remove the provider's.

C.text: It replaces the need to measure performance
C.rationale: Qualitative feedback and quantitative measures are complementary.

D.text: It should only be gathered at the end of the relationship
D.rationale: Late feedback reduces the opportunity to improve value during consumption.

257.question_text: Which statement best describes artificial intelligence?
257.explanation: Artificial intelligence refers to technologies capable of performing tasks normally associated with human intelligence, notably learning, reasoning, recognising patterns, or understanding language. It is not limited to following a fixed sequence of rules.

A.text: Technologies capable of performing tasks normally associated with human intelligence
A.rationale: This answer covers the general scope of AI without reducing it to a particular type of model.

B.text: Any automation running a fully predefined sequence of rules
B.rationale: A deterministic automation can operate without learning or reasoning capabilities.

C.text: Only systems capable of generating text and images
C.rationale: Generative AI is one category of AI and not its full definition.

D.text: Only physical robots capable of working without humans
D.rationale: AI can be purely software and retain various levels of human oversight.

258.scenario: Two companies use the same AI tool. The first runs a few isolated trials; the second has a strategy, reliable data, skills, controls, and uses embedded in operations.
258.question_text: Which concept mainly explains their difference?
258.explanation: AI maturity describes the extent to which an organisation can use AI effectively, responsibly, consistently, and in an integrated way to support its objectives. It depends notably on governance, data, skills, and processes.

A.text: AI maturity
A.rationale: The difference concerns the organisational ability to adopt and govern AI sustainably.

B.text: The model's compute power
B.rationale: The companies use the same tool; their difference comes from their organisational capabilities.

C.text: The type of service relationship
C.rationale: The relationship with a supplier is not enough to explain the internal integration of AI.

D.text: The number of outputs produced by the tool
D.rationale: Usage volume does not demonstrate effective, responsible, and consistent adoption.

259.question_text: Which pairing of a lifecycle activity with an AI use is the most appropriate?
259.explanation: AI can support every lifecycle activity when it is used with appropriate controls. Uses must match the activity's objective rather than being applied without connection to the work performed.

A.text: Discover: analyse needs trends; build: assist testing; operate: detect anomalies; support: suggest solutions
A.rationale: Each proposed use directly supports the objective of the corresponding activity.

B.text: Discover: close incidents; build: negotiate SLAs; operate: define the mission; support: select the strategy
B.rationale: These uses do not match the objectives of the activities listed.

C.text: Acquire: remove any supplier evaluation; transition: ignore impacts; deliver: avoid feedback
C.rationale: AI does not justify removing necessary controls and learning.

D.text: Use AI only in the build activity, because other activities do not concern technology
D.rationale: AI can support analysis, design, operation, delivery, and support, among other activities.

260.question_text: Which definition best matches a value chain in ITIL Foundation Version 5?
260.explanation: A value chain is a system of interconnected activities an organisation uses to create and deliver products and services and to co-create value. It is executed through value streams adapted to demands and opportunities.

A.text: A system of interconnected activities used to create and deliver products and services and co-create value
A.rationale: This definition covers the overall activity system and its purpose of value creation.
