B.text: A single procedure executed in the same order for every request
B.rationale: Value streams can combine the activities in different ways depending on context.

C.text: An inventory of the organisation's technologies and suppliers
C.rationale: An inventory describes resources and does not represent the activity system that creates value.

D.text: A list of the metrics contained in the service level agreements
D.rationale: Metrics can evaluate some outcomes but do not constitute the value chain.

261.scenario: An organisation has a clear purpose, but its value chain activities and practices are organised inconsistently with it.
261.question_text: Which role should the operating model mainly play?
261.explanation: The operating model translates purpose and strategy into a coherent organisation of capabilities, resources, activities, and practices. It explains how the organisation concretely works to create value.

A.text: Link purpose to the value chain activities and the practices needed to execute it
A.rationale: The operating model turns the organisation's direction into a coherent way of working.

B.text: Replace purpose with a list of procedures
B.rationale: Procedures support execution, but they do not replace the organisation's fundamental contribution.

C.text: Keep activities and practices independent of strategy
C.rationale: This separation produces exactly the misalignment described.

D.text: Define only the technology architecture
D.rationale: The operating model also covers people, partners, flows, decisions, and other capabilities.

262.scenario: A team prepares a value stream map showing only the steps and their total duration.
262.question_text: Which additional elements would mainly make the map more useful for improvement?
262.explanation: A value stream map can show inputs, outputs, triggers, stakeholders, processing and waiting times, handoffs, loops, controls, information, and measures. These elements help understand the end-to-end flow and its obstacles.

A.text: The triggers, inputs, outputs, handoffs, loops, stakeholders, information, and measures of the stream
A.rationale: These elements let you analyse dependencies, rework, decisions, and contributions to value.

B.text: Only the job titles of leaders
B.rationale: Hierarchy alone does not describe the actual flow of work and information.

C.text: Only the annual budget of each department
C.rationale: Budget can provide context, but does not sufficiently complete the flow representation.

D.text: Only the list of applications owned by the organisation
D.rationale: Tools show neither waits, handoffs, nor loops of the stream.

263.scenario: An organisation must coordinate a temporary initiative with deliverables, a budget, dependencies, and a precise deadline to modify several products and services.
263.question_text: Why is project management important in an ITIL environment?
263.explanation: Project management provides structured coordination to deliver temporary changes within the agreed limits. ITIL then helps align those deliverables with value, governance, the lifecycle, and ongoing activities.

A.text: It coordinates the temporary delivery of changes that must integrate with products, services, and operations
A.rationale: Project management organises the initiative, while ITIL links its results to the permanent management system.

B.text: It replaces every lifecycle activity for the duration of the project
B.rationale: Lifecycle activities remain necessary to design, build, transition, and support the outcomes.

C.text: It guarantees that every project automatically creates value
C.rationale: A project can meet its constraints while failing to produce the expected outcomes.

D.text: It only serves to produce reports for governance
D.rationale: Reporting is useful, but the practice mostly covers planning, coordination, and delivery of the project.

264.scenario: A DevOps team automates its pipeline and delivers frequently. It wants to link these deliveries to stakeholder needs, governance controls, and operational support.
264.question_text: How should ITIL and DevOps concretely collaborate?
264.explanation: DevOps improves collaboration, automation, feedback, and flow between development and operations. ITIL provides the value context, lifecycle activities, practices, governance, and relationships needed to integrate that flow into overall operation.

A.text: Use DevOps to accelerate flow and feedback, and ITIL to align them on value, governance, practices, and the lifecycle
A.rationale: The two approaches play complementary roles in the same management system.

B.text: Use DevOps only for development and ITIL only after each incident
B.rationale: ITIL covers the whole lifecycle and DevOps goes beyond the development activity alone.

C.text: Remove ITIL controls so DevOps can deploy without any constraint
C.rationale: Speed must remain aligned with risk, value, and governance requirements.

D.text: Create two separate value chains with no data exchange or feedback
D.rationale: This separation would destroy exactly the collaboration and end-to-end flow being sought.
